grants.name: Small Business Revitalization (SBR) Grant Program
grants.organization: Georgia Coalition of Black Chambers (GCBC) & Advancing Black Businesses Foundation
grants.eligibility: Georgia-based for-profit small businesses, with targeted support for Black-owned and historically under-resourced enterprises across Georgia. Requires completion of a business development/financial education component (such as the FDIC Money Smart curriculum).
grants.description: Pairs non-dilutive capital grants with structured business education and growth coaching specifically for Georgia small businesses. Fast Apparel is uniquely positioned to apply for funds to scale commercial Ultra HD DTF production equipment, expand local warehouse blank inventory, and hire seasonal print technicians.

grants.name: Tory Burch Foundation Fellows Program
grants.eligibility: Woman-owned (51%+), for-profit, U.S.-based business generating at least $75,000 in annual revenue. Founder must be 21+ and hold significant day-to-day management authority. Free application.
grants.description: A prestigious national fellowship providing a $2,000 non-dilutive grant, 1-on-1 executive coaching, workshops, and high-level founder networking. Fast Apparel can leverage this fellowship to expand executive operations, corporate client partnerships, and direct-to-consumer e-commerce expansion.

grants.name: NASE Growth Grants
grants.eligibility: Micro-businesses and self-employed entrepreneurs who are NASE members in good standing. Funds can be used for marketing, equipment, software, or workspace expansion. Requires statement of use, business plan, and financial statement.
grants.description: Awarded quarterly specifically to finance targeted equipment purchases or marketing campaigns. Fast Apparel can apply directly for commercial heat platen attachments, high-speed dual heat presses, or targeted digital ad spend across Metro Atlanta.

grants.name: The Amber Grant
grants.eligibility: At least 50% women-owned businesses based in the United States or Canada, ranging from startup stage to established operating businesses. Application is quick and evaluated on community passion and business vision.
grants.description: A long-running, trusted monthly grant recognizing entrepreneurial passion and community impact with no rigid balance sheet restrictions. Fast Apparel can highlight women-led operations and utilize the capital for seasonal garment blank stocking and rush fulfillment infrastructure.

grants.name: Invest Atlanta Small Business Improvement Grant (SBIG)
grants.organization: Invest Atlanta (City of Atlanta Economic Development Authority)
grants.eligibility: Operating small businesses or commercial property owners located within designated City of Atlanta Tax Allocation Districts (TADs); facilities under 15,000 sq ft; eligible for interior and exterior physical capital improvements.
grants.description: Provides up to $50,000 for physical facility and workspace buildouts, electrical infrastructure upgrades, and commercial exterior signage. Fast Apparel can strategically apply to fund industrial power drops and ventilation installations for high-volume commercial DTF printers and heat presses in Atlanta.
